title: Go net SplitHostPort and JoinHostPort: retain input on parse failure
applies_when: Go endpoint normalization adds a default port after net.SplitHostPort returns an error, especially when a short declaration shadows the original host.
lesson: Do not use the failed parser's host output as the original address. Retain the input separately and inspect the endpoint stored by the real client, not a copied normalization expression. For already URL-validated bracketed IPv6 inputs, remove the existing brackets before JoinHostPort so brackets are not duplicated. Include explicit-port controls and mixed endpoint lists. A matching error symptom in an issue is not causal evidence: inspect its exact supplied address and advertised endpoints before linking a fix.
avoid_when: An explicit port bypasses this default-port branch. JuiceFS issue6057 already uses :2379 and advertises 0.0.0.0, so it does not validate the omitted-port diagnosis. Bracket trimming is not general malformed-address validation. These tests construct and close the actual etcd client but do not prove live cluster connectivity, metadata transactions, all core tests, or maintainer acceptance.

evidence.note: Unchanged producer overwrites the loop host with SplitHostPort's failed output before adding 2379.

Seven actual-client endpoint cases: five fail with unchanged production, two explicit-port controls pass before and after; all pass after, including five race repeats on Linux/Go1.25.10. Full core testing was blocked by absent Redis.

The reporter provides an explicit port and an all-interface advertised address. This contradicts using that issue as proof of the omitted-port bug; it does not resolve the reported connectivity problem.
Submitted correction and English/Chinese default-port documentation. Publication is not CI/review acceptance or a performance result.
